title: Our Week in Faro: A Peek Into Junction’s 2026 Offsite
summary: 47 Junctionistas, four days in Faro, one boat ride too many for some. A week-in-the-life look at our 2026 company offsite.
body_markdown:
## Hi 👋 I’m Nicole from Junction’s Talent team


#### On the last week of September, 47 of us Junctionistas *(Junctionauts? Junctionites? We haven’t come up with a name yet and are currently accepting suggestions)* traveled to Faro, Portugal for our annual company offsite. It was my first offsite with Junction, and honestly, will probably go down as the best offsite of my life. I want to take you along for the week!


### **Sunday**


Everyone arrives in Portugal, jet lagged and worse for wear; meeting ~20 of your coworkers in person for the first time after 18 hours of travel isn’t necessarily recommended.


After check in, it was time to explore the hotel. I don’t want to rub it in, but let’s just say I had multiple ‘pinch me’ moments. I’ll let you hear it from one of my colleagues:


> “The resort we stayed at was beyond stunning. From the rolling hills surrounding the resort, to the well maintained golf course on the grounds, to the breathtaking sunsets and moonlit nights - it was just perfect.”


After a few hours of R&R (read: nap) it was time for our first company dinner. All of our dinners were assigned seating, which, I know: ugh, but I changed my mind five minutes into that first dinner. Throughout our four days together, I got to spend lots of quality time with people I’ve never interacted with before. I was convinced to travel to Scotland, heard about a celebrity interaction with an Affleck, and spent way too much time showing pictures of my dog.


The highlight of the night was hilarious pub trivia hosted by our Head of Engineering, Mark. Mark dubbed real voices of our employees so they were speaking in a different language; I’ve never wondered what our Head of CS would sound like speaking Italian, but now I know.


### **Monday**


Monday was the start of our working sessions, and we kicked off by setting the stage: where we’ve been and where we’re going. We’re a vastly different, and much bigger, company since we launched our Operating Principles (our version of company values), and they were ripe for a refresh. Our Founder/CEO Maitham[shared a new version](https://app.notion.com/p/junction-api/Operating-Principles-3ded9955818e80b8b539f261b8e81d40) with us. When done well, I believe strongly that these values help you prioritize your trajectory as a company and identify the best people to get you there. It’s been fun to see how these new principles have seeped their way into our culture over the past few weeks!


After our session came my favorite part of the week: an unreal boat ride around the Algarve. If you could close your eyes and picture (well, maybe not actually close them - this isn’t an auditory medium): warm sun hitting your skin, gorgeous blue waters, and the sound of light house music in the background. In one word: perfection. Just don’t ask the five Junctionistas who spent two hours seasick 🥴


### **Tuesday**


Tuesday was my favorite day of working sessions, focused on shipping fast. The highlight of the morning was an hourlong “Build It” session, where each cross-functional table was assigned a task to push live in 60 minutes. While my table focused on improving our employer branding efforts (you didn’t think it was random that I’m writing this blog, right?! 😇), other groups shipped major features that positively impacted both our customers and internal team.


I walked away from our Build It session so inspired; working at a company without red tape lends itself to making impact *quick* , and it was exhilarating to see what we could accomplish when sitting with a table of smart folks excited to take it on.


In the afternoon, we were able to channel our competitive energy into a sports day, where we were pitted against each other for fun field day-esque games like holding an egg on a spoon. My green team might not have won on paper, but they won in my heart 💚


### **Wednesday**


Our last day of the offsite was a memorable one. Our group session was focused on our impact, and as a mission-based company, it is something we all deeply resonate with. Our ‘day job’ ultimately saves lives, and every single role at the company plays a part in that mission. It’s a cool thing to spend your workweek doing something that can (and hopefully will) positively impact the health of you or someone you know - not a lot of people get to say that.


We ended the day with an incredible rooftop dinner. We had an awards ceremony for my outstanding colleagues who go above and beyond every day, and even had an astronomer show us a crazy view of Saturn.


On the flight home, I couldn’t help but feel truly grateful. Every time you join a new company, you take a risk that it’s not as advertised or you won’t fit in. But my six months at Junction have proven to be so much more than I could’ve imagined.


I’ve learned SO much. Like holy cow, so much. Working with really smart people does that to you - it’s like symbiosis of some kind. I’m honored to be considered a Junctionista amongst some of the smartest people I’ve ever met.
